reuse.why: The API reuses getApproxNumberThreshold but introduces getExpectedScheduleAmount instead of extending and calling the existing shared getScheduledAmount.

duplication.why: The new API helper duplicates the shared helper's missing-value handling, numeric dispatch, and range endpoint selection.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules.ts alongside getScheduledAmount, rather than in the API serialization module.

scope.why: All edits concern expected schedule amounts, their API representation, associated comments, or focused tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must now coordinate two amount-policy implementations, with approximate-amount policy available only through the API-specific helper.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/api-models.ts: scheduleModel.toExternal calls the new private getExpectedScheduleAmount instead of the existing shared getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount reshapes getScheduledAmount's missing/number/range dispatch under a new name, repeating range selection while adding API-local approximate handling.

abstraction_drift.where: The API's new expectedAmount consumer bypasses shared getScheduledAmount; approximate policy accumulates in its private replacement rather than extending the shared definition.
